issues.body: `heads_name_party_collection` defines collection-ness as `party_collection_members(h)` being non-empty. That cannot distinguish a plain party IRI from a PartyCollection for which this request supplied zero membership edges. Consequently, a collection-valued prohibition with no evidence bypasses the one-shot fallback and persists only the collection IRI as a deny head; member sessions match by identity alone and escape the deny. The same flaw affects an ALLOW `neq`/`isNoneOf` collection carve-out: it persists an exception matcher for the collection IRI that excludes no member, widening the grant. This contradicts the stated fail-closed invariant and is especially important because the public API explicitly documents empty results for both cases.
issues.fix_hint: Carry explicit collection identity/type information separately from the member list (for example, request-supplied known PartyCollection IRIs or policy type metadata) and use that for the DENY/carve-out fallback decision; do not infer collection-ness from a non-empty edge set. Add real enforcement-path tests for a collection-valued prohibition and collection carve-out with zero supplied membership edges, showing that no conditional deny/grant is emitted and no unrelated/member session is widened.
issues.title: Collection safety check fails when membership evidence is empty

verdict.summary: The ALLOW expansion is narrowly tested, but the fail-closed DENY/carve-out guard only recognizes a collection when this particular request supplies at least one membership edge for that head. With absent evidence (and likewise when a caller knows the IRI is a PartyCollection but supplies no member edge), the new code emits the unsafe persisted condition it says must be avoided. The added tests cover the positive-evidence case and therefore miss this fail-open path.
